q: In your own words: why does a rule you put in CLAUDE.md apply to every turn of a Claude Code session?
correct: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md automatically when the session starts and keeps it in the context window, so the rule is in front of the model on every turn.

misconceptions.label: Believes CLAUDE.md trains, fine-tunes or permanently changes the model itself.
Believes you must paste, mention or @-reference CLAUDE.md in each prompt for it to apply.
Believes Claude remembers CLAUDE.md like a person, across all projects and sessions, rather than reading it fresh at the start of each session.
Believes CLAUDE.md rules are enforced like code or configuration, so the model cannot ignore them.

rubric: Says it applies but gives no reason
Says the file is read or loaded, but not when or where it lives
Explains it is loaded into the context window at session start, so it is present on every turn
why: CLAUDE.md is loaded into the context window when a session starts. Every turn sees it because it is part of the context, not because the model learned it — which is also why a very long session or a conflicting instruction can crowd it out.
